newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eurowings/Air France to fly Frankfurt-Berlin.
newsitem.headline: Eurowings/Air France to fly Frankfurt-Berlin.

text.p: German airline Eurowings Luftverkehrs AG and partner Air France are to take on Deutsche Lufthansa AG on one of its last domestic monopoly routes.
Eurowings said it will fly a code-share service with Air France four times a day between Frankfurt and the Berlin city centre airport Tempelhof with a turboprop ATR-72 from May 5.
An Air France statement said the French carrier would have a limited seat alloment on the flight and its frequent flyers would earn mileage points.
Lufthansa executives have previously said that the airline makes a loss on the route. It is the only airline on the route with 16 daily flights with estimated 1.4 million travellers a year.
Last month the German cartel office ordered Lufthansa to cut "excessive" fares of more than 800 marks on the route following a probe into price levels on the domestic air travel market.
Eurowings chairman Reinhard Santner said: "There is a need for a second carrier. We think we will be successful on the route."
The airline will charge a one-way super saver fare of 119 marks and have one-way business fares as low as 239 marks, undercutting Lufthansa full return prices by more than 300 marks.

Marketing director Ulrich Sigman said the carrier would have less than 10 per cent of capacity but aimed to seize at least a 10 per cent market share and even more of the lucrative business travel segment.
Air France will also add a fifth daily Berlin Tegel to Paris Charles de Gaulle flight from March 30, it said.

Eurowings managed to get four slots at crowded Frankfurt airport and then swopped them with several airlines including Air France and Delta Air Lines to get the right departure times, industry sources told Reuters.
Lufthansa sales and marketing chief executive Hemjoe Klein told an ITB news conference that he "welcomed competition" but declined to say how Lufthansa would react.

But he added: "There is no monopoly between Frankfurt and Berlin. There is only one airline which has committed itself to intensive services on the route." -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
